deviations.from: Structured-task final part originally asked about experimental repeats under the task’s AO1/AO2 labels.
deviations.to: Consequential inference about unsupported 12 h extrapolation from the supplied 0–4 h data.
deviations.why: Keeps the structured activity’s reasoning demand in B; practical repeat/method evaluation remains C in the separate practical task and slots.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the increase in mass when a seed sample changes from 42 g to 57 g.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 57 − 42 = 15 g; the sample gained 15 g.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete this record: a culture contains 180 cells initially and 240 cells later. Change in cell number: __; direction of change: __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 240 − 180 = 60 cells; an increase.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the mean of three leaf lengths: 21 mm, 24 mm and 27 mm.
Complete the comparison: group A leaf lengths are 10, 12 and 14 mm; group B lengths are 11, 12 and 13 mm. Their means are __; the group with the smaller spread is __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Both means are 12 mm. Group B has the smaller spread, so its readings are more consistent.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the loss in mass from 3.75 g to 3.20 g.
Complete the statement using readings 0.45 g, 0.9 g and 0.72 g: the largest mass is __ and the smallest is __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Largest 0.9 g; smallest 0.45 g. The extra decimal digit in 0.45 does not make it the larger value.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate three fifths of a sample of 50 seeds.
Complete the sample comparison: 8 of 32 seedlings wilt. The simplified wilted fraction is __ and the unwilted fraction is __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Wilted 1/4; unwilted 3/4, because 24 of the 32 seedlings did not wilt.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the percentage germination when 36 of 48 seeds germinate.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 36 ÷ 48 × 100 = 75 percent germination.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete the interpretation: a tissue sample rises from 20 g to 25 g. Its gain is __ percent, and its final mass is __ percent of its initial mass.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Gain 25 percent; final mass 125 percent of the initial mass.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the simplest green:yellow seed ratio from 42 green and 14 yellow seeds.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 42:14 simplifies to 3:1 by dividing both counts by 14.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete the interpretation of a black:white ratio of 2:1 in a sample of 60 seeds: black __; white __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 40 black and 20 white; the ratio contains three parts in total.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate reciprocal time for a fixed endpoint reached in 25 s.
Complete the comparison for the same fixed endpoint: A takes 10 s and B takes 20 s. Their reciprocal times are __ and __. The relative rate of A is __ times the relative rate of B.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A: 0.1 s⁻¹; B: 0.05 s⁻¹. A has 2 times the relative rate of B because it reaches the same endpoint in half the time.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the volume delivered in 12 s if a pump supplies 3 cm³ each second at a constant rate.
Complete the classification: a fixed 24 cm³ is delivered at 2 cm³/s in 12 s and at 4 cm³/s in 6 s. Rate and time are __ proportional because their product is __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Inversely proportional; the product is 24 cm³ in both trials.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the volume of a cube with side length 3 mm.
Complete the comparison: one square face has side 2 mm and another has side 4 mm. Their areas are __ and __. The larger area is __ times the smaller area.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 4 mm² and 16 mm². The larger area is 4 times the smaller area, because doubling the side multiplies the area by 2 × 2.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate y when x = yz, x is 84 and z is 7.
Complete the interpretation: final mass = initial mass + gain. Final mass is 13 g and gain is 5 g. Initial mass is __; this is the mass __ the gain.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Initial mass is 8 g; the mass before the gain.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest which source best supports a comparison of seedling water use: A gives total water for 20 seedlings over five days; B describes leaf colour; C gives total water but no seedling number or duration. Explain your choice.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A supplies the volume, sample size and time needed for a fair comparison. B measures a different feature and C lacks the denominators needed to compare use per seedling per day.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete the x-axis and y-axis labels for plotting paired readings of chosen soaking duration in hours and measured seedling length in millimetres.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: x: soaking duration / h; y: seedling length / mm. These use the same quantities and units as the corresponding table headings.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete a table heading for masses 2.1, 2.3 and 2.5, all measured in grams, and explain what the heading tells the reader.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Mass / g; each numerical reading is a mass in grams.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Explain the problem if one learner records a root as 35 mm and another as 3.5 cm, then averages 35 and 3.5 without conversion.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Averaging 35 and 3.5 gives 19.25, which is neither mm nor cm and does not describe the root, because the two numbers are in different units. Converting both to 35 mm gives a mean of 35 mm, since the two learners actually measured the same length.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete the mean column for repeat shoot increases of 4, 6 and 8 mm, and state what that entry represents.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Mean increase 6 mm; it summarises the three repeat increases under that condition.

ao_demand_evidence.input: A learner’s observation times run from 0 to 80 s. Complete the x-axis labels 0, __, __, __, 80 using equal intervals, and state the size of each interval.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 0, 20, 40, 60, 80. Each interval is 20 s, because the labels rise in equal steps.

ao_demand_evidence.input: On graph paper, draw a graph of these readings for two shoots. Time / min: 0, 2, 4. Shoot A length / mm: 10, 14, 18. Shoot B length / mm: 10, 12, 14. Choose the axes and scales yourself and label both lines.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Time / min goes on the x-axis and shoot length / mm on the y-axis. Plot A at (0,10), (2,14), (4,18) and B at (0,10), (2,12), (4,14) on regular scales. Each set lies on a straight line, so join each with a ruled line, and label the lines A and B.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Label a horizontal axis for elapsed seconds and a vertical axis for seedling height measured in millimetres, and give the resulting title.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Horizontal: time / s. Vertical: seedling height / mm. Title: seedling height against time.

ao_demand_evidence.input: On graph paper, plot these practical results: chosen temperature / °C: 10, 20, 30; measured endpoint time / s: 80, 40, 20. Draw and label the axes with units, choose the scales, draw a smooth curve through the points and give a title.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Temperature is the independent variable, so it goes on the x-axis; endpoint time goes on the y-axis. Label them temperature / °C and endpoint time / s. Plot (10,80), (20,40) and (30,20) on regular scales. The points do not lie on a straight line, so draw a smooth curve through them, falling less steeply as temperature rises. Title: endpoint time against temperature.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Complete the plotting instructions: for the first data set use small __ or __; explain why a large blob is unsuitable.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Small crosses or encircled dots; a blob hides the exact coordinate and makes the reading uncertain.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Label a suitable title and both axes for readings of root length in mm taken at successive days.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Title: root length against time. x: time / days. y: root length / mm.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest a justified conclusion from this growth record: day 0, 12 mm; day 2, 17 mm; day 4, 20 mm.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The plant length increased over the four days, but the two-day gain fell from 5 mm to 3 mm, so the rate of length increase slowed.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the total surface area of a cube with side length 2 mm.
Complete the conversions: 2 cm² = __ mm² and 2 cm³ = __ mm³.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 200 mm² and 2000 mm³. The conversion factors are squared for area and cubed for volume.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Explain why a cube doubled in side length has less surface area per unit volume even though its total area rises.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Doubling length multiplies area by four but volume by eight. Volume therefore increases faster, so the surface-area-to-volume ratio halves.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the length in micrometres of a structure measured as 0.32 mm.
Complete the comparison: A is 1500 μm long, B is 2 mm long. A in millimetres is __; the longer structure is __.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A is 1.5 mm; B is longer by 0.5 mm.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Explain the error when a learner divides an image length of 8 mm by an actual length of 40 μm and reports magnification as 0.2.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The lengths were not converted to the same unit. 8 mm is 8000 μm, so the magnification is 8000 ÷ 40 = 200, written ×200.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the ordinary decimal value of 3.2 × 10³ cells.
Complete the conversion: 0.0007 m = __ × 10⁻⁴ m. State whether this length is positive or negative.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 7 × 10⁻⁴ m. The length is positive; the negative power only shows that it is a small fraction of a metre.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest why a single plant growing faster in a warm room than a single plant in a cool room does not establish a temperature effect.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Individual plants vary naturally, so the warm-room plant may simply have grown faster anyway; one plant per room gives no idea of that variation. The two rooms may also differ in other ways, such as light or watering, so the difference may be caused by something other than temperature.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest a conclusion for germination of 40, 65 and 80 percent after soaking for 0, 2 and 4 h respectively.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Within 0–4 h, longer soaking was associated with higher germination, from 40 to 80 percent. The conclusion applies only over that range.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest the next action when a leaf count of 90 differs sharply from repeat counts of 18, 19 and 20 for comparable samples.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Because 90 is far from 18, 19 and 20, investigate it. Check the original record for a copying slip, check that the right sample was counted, and repeat the count. Do not replace 90 with a nearby value without evidence.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Discuss the trend in these shoot lengths: day 0, 10 mm; day 2, 18 mm; day 4, 21 mm; day 6, 21 mm.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Length rises from 10 mm to 21 mm over the first four days. The gain is 8 mm in the first two days and 3 mm in the next two, so growth slows. Between days 4 and 6 the length stays at 21 mm, so growth has stopped, but the length has not fallen.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest why “the plant shrank after day 2” is wrong when lengths were 8 mm on day 0, 16 mm on day 2 and 19 mm on day 4.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Length still rose from 16 to 19 mm. The smaller gain shows slower growth, not shrinkage.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest a precaution when a learner must compare three volumes accurately but the measuring cylinder is standing on a sloping bench.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Move the cylinder to a level surface and read at eye level. The tilted arrangement makes the meniscus hard to align consistently with the scale.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest a reasoned prediction when seeds are placed on dry paper and on equally warm moist paper, with oxygen available in both.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: More seeds are expected to germinate on the moist paper because water is needed for germination and the dry treatment lacks it.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest why an investigation comparing warm and cool tubes needs a thermometer rather than relying on hand temperature.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A thermometer gives a numerical temperature for each treatment; touch is subjective and does not establish the actual temperature difference.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest a conclusion when equal groups of seeds at the same temperature give 10 percent germination without water and 85 percent with water, with oxygen available in both.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Germination was 85 percent with water but only 10 percent without it, so these results support the idea that seeds need water to germinate.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Fig. VIS-6116-1.2.6-12 is a photograph of a specimen. Draw a large line drawing of it, label the main visible structures and give the drawing a title.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A good answer uses clear continuous lines with no shading. It shows only what can be seen in the photograph, with the parts in the same proportions. Ruled label lines end on the structures they name, and a title names the specimen.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the magnification of a 24 mm drawing of a specimen whose actual length is 0.6 mm.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: 24 ÷ 0.6 = 40; magnification ×40.
